<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /meta/view/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via /meta/view/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via /forms/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx`  _(via /meta/view/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via /forms/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /forms/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /meta/view/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`  _(via /forms/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via /forms/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /meta/view/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /meta/view/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7f96d225d686fc8235bacc55939d51c528e1441f` — the merge of head `cc016f8ac169871c2d11e356b6cf186ccc7210af` into base `bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7f96d225d686fc8235bacc55939d51c528e1441f && git checkout 7f96d225d686fc8235bacc55939d51c528e1441f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0 cc016f8ac169871c2d11e356b6cf186ccc7210af && git checkout -B drift-repro bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0 && git merge --no-ff cc016f8ac169871c2d11e356b6cf186ccc7210af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读
- 校验规则不再把「被表单类动作按名字打开的默认/新建表单」报成「内部表单、不再加载」;这类表单用户其实还能打开,原警告说错了。

- 这是一条只给警告的规则,改动只会少报,不会拦下或放行任何东西;可直接撤回。
- 无需你操作。

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** at head `cc016f8ac169871c2d11e356b6cf186ccc7210af` (read 2026-11-24T00:48Z).

1. **Shape.** Open, draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #36545`, no closing keyword anywhere: right, the card's rail half moved to #36797 and its prose and checklist re-audits to #36798 (seat comment 7118012396), so this PR delivers the lint half plus N3's comment fixes only.
2. **Premise measured.** `origin/main`: `validate-internal-form-views.ts` reports every non-public default and create form with no look at actions. The head's exemption matches the Console path the rule's message is about (a `type: 'form'` action's literal `target` → `/forms/NAME` → `/meta/view/NAME`), by EQUAL served name. Seat check of the pairing: `servedFormNames` re-runs the spec's `expandViewContainer` on the object `deriveViewContainerObject` binds and pairs the non-default form items with `formViews` entries by order; the expansion (`view.zod.ts`, form family) emits exactly the object-valued `formViews` entries in key order, then `form` as the one `isDefault` item, so the pairing holds today, collisions included. N3: `git grep resolveFormViewLayout -- ui docs/qa` on the head finds only two historical `CHANGELOG.md` entries.
3. **Gates at this head (check-runs).** 59 success · 10 expected skip · 0 unexpected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`. The dev's local `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED is answered by CI's Type Check lanes at this head.
4. **Accepted deviations.** Changeset flag from `l1-face`: `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/plugin-form` are touched without an entry. Read: every change there is a comment (`FormPage.tsx`) or a test file (`FormPage.visibleWhen.test.tsx`, three `plugin-form/src/__tests__` files); both packages ship `dist` only (`files[]`), so nothing they publish moves and no entry is owed. Tests: ablation of the guard fails the three exemption cases with the CONTROL (short, interpolated, non-form target) green. Changeset read sentence by sentence against the diff: true. Nit, accepted as is: `servedFormNames` re-derives the expansion's `formViews` skip test and pairs by position, so it is a second copy of the expansion's order; a key carried on `ExpandedViewItem` would remove that, but it is a spec change outside this card.
5. **Out of scope.** Owned elsewhere already: the rail half (#36797) and the re-audits (#36798). The showcase allow-list row for `showcase_task · form` is removed and the two-way advisory test now pins the rule's silence there. `Skills-docs:` not owed.
6. **Landing.** **Clause-② question answered: `no` is right.** The rule is advisory: it raises a `warning`, never refuses, so reporting fewer cases moves no accepted set and no published contract; `Metadata-protocol: none` holds too (an author can write exactly what they could). No contract face (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path), so no L2 is owed; this record is the review of record at `TIER_DEFAULT`. `Part of` keeps #36545 open: after the merge the seat removes `pm:dispatched` by hand (landing rule B) and closes #36545 pointing at #36797 and #36798, since nothing else is left on it. Land on this head, or on a main-sync head after a delta read.
